 versus

 Through: Mr. Umesh Kumar and Ms. Sakshi
 Mishra, Advs. for R-1.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Tara Vitasta Ganju
 Order
% 08.10.2025 CM Appl. 62944/2025[Seeking condonation of delay in filing]
1. This is an Application filed on behalf of the Appellant seeking condonation of delay of 120 days in filing the present Appeal.
2. Learned Counsel for the Respondent No. 1 submits that he has no objection if the prayers made in the present Application are allowed.
3. Accordingly, the delay is condoned.
The Application stands disposed of.

CM Appl. 62943/2025[Exemption from filing certified copy of the order dated 11.03.2025]
4. Allowed, subject to the Appellant certified copy of the order dated 11.03.2025 within a period of three weeks.
5. The Application stands disposed of.

MAC.APP. 650/2025 & CM Appl. 62942/2025[Stay]
6. The present Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [hereinafter referred to as "MV Act"] impugning the Award dated 11.03.2025 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, MACT
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/10/2025 at 22:09:37 (SE), Saket Courts, New Delhi [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"].

By the Impugned Award, the compensation amount in the sum of Rs. 50,75,016/- along with interest at the rate of 9%
per annum has been awarded.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that the challenge in the present Appeal is on two grounds.

Firstly, he submits that no evidence was led in the matter and secondly, he submits that the findings recorded in the Detailed Accident Report (DAR), although records the consent of the Appellant, no consent given by the Appellant in this behalf.
8. Learned Counsel seeks to rely upon certain documents in support of this contention.

However,
the relevant documents have not been filed by the Appellant.
Learned Counsel for the Appellant requests for some time to place on record the documents in support of his contentions.
9. Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1, who appears on advance service, submits that he has not received a copy of the complete paper book.
Let a copy of the complete set of the paper book be supplied to the learned Counsel for Respondent No. 1 within two days under acknowledgment.

10. At request, list on 04.11.2025.
11.
In the meantime, the Registry is directed to place on record the digital copy of the Trial Court Record duly paginated and book-marked in accordance with the rules of the High Court.
12. The parties will act based on the digitally signed copy of the order.
TARA VITASTA GANJU, J OCTOBER 8, 2025/r
